summary: Per-host transcript-to-evidence extractors with tier classification (edit/read/gs/mention). Host gotchas verified on real transcripts: Cursor's conversation JSONL has NO tool_result records, so its extractor trusts calls and compensates with a stat-existence check on EVERY claim; Codex pairs custom_tool_call to output by call_id (result-confirmed) and its exec input embeds shell as tools.exec_command with the cmd key appearing BOTH quoted and unquoted across rollout versions. Default-deny: an unknown bash verb contributes at most a mention. Reading through the SHELL counts as reading: read verbs by name, plus inline scripts in any language (node -e, python3 -c, php -r, heredocs) matched on the file-open call in their body, since with an inline flag that body is in the command string; a script FILE stays a mention because its body is invisible. Measured on 2961 local transcripts while adding this: attributing the whole command would have over-tiered 50.6% of real inline reads (they carry unrelated path tokens), and output VOLUME was rejected as a precision criterion because cat's median output is 18 lines against an inline script's 10 — the distributions do not separate.

summary: Per-host transcript-to-evidence extractors with tier classification (edit/read/gs/mention), and the one table deciding what shell activity counts as reading or writing a file. Host gotchas verified on real transcripts: Cursor's conversation JSONL has NO tool_result records, so its extractor trusts calls and compensates with a stat-existence check on EVERY claim; Codex pairs custom_tool_call to output by call_id and its exec input embeds shell with the cmd key appearing BOTH quoted and unquoted across rollout versions. Default-deny: an unknown bash verb contributes at most a mention. Reading through the SHELL counts as reading (read verbs, plus inline scripts in any language matched on the file-open call in their body); writing through the shell counts as writing (bashEditTargets: redirect, tee, sed -i, literal write arg). A heredoc tag is an ARBITRARY identifier — the old EOF/PY/JS whitelist missed PATCH, TS and MSG and made those scripts invisible to both surfaces. redirectTargets overrides the verb table so `cat > x <<EOF` is an edit, not a read. Measured while building this: attributing a whole command would over-tier 50.6% of inline reads; output VOLUME does not separate reads from searches (cat's median is 18 lines vs an inline script's 10); and the deterministic write rules cover 89.2% of shell writes, so the single-literal guess for computed paths was rejected at 5.8% marginal gain.
